title: Custom Global Actors
hints: `@globalActor` turns an actor with a `static let shared` into an attribute.
Put `@AnalyticsActor` on the class, the logging function and a runner; call the runner with `await`.
Within `@AnalyticsActor` code, `log(e, to: tracker)` needs no `await`.
jsBridge: `@globalActor` creates a named isolation domain like `@MainActor`, but for your own subsystem (analytics, database). Everything annotated with it runs serialised on that actor. JS has no analogue, since there's only one thread there.

compass.q: A dedicated Web Worker for analytics is the closest JS analogue. How is a global actor lighter?
Custom global actor vs a plain `actor` instance: when do you want the annotation-based isolation?
Calling `@AnalyticsActor` code from `@MainActor` code needs `await`. Why?
Would you create global actors in an app, or is `@MainActor` + plain actors enough?
